general_information.Description: This course provides an introduction to the fundamental techniques and principles needed for working with audio devices (microphones, mixers, etc.) and audio-editing applications such as Adobe Audition. Students will learn how to record audio, perform voice-over, create foley, and edit and mix sound for various media formats, including short films, animated films, TVCs, and viral videos. As a multimedia course, students will develop an understanding of sound aesthetics, musicality, vocal performance, and critical listening. Through regular listening exercises and class critiques, students will enhance their ability to analyze and evaluate sound in different media products. The course also introduces students to AI tools that support audio processing and voice simulation (text-to-speech), helping them optimize their workflow during production. Objective: Upon completing this course, students will be able to create soundtracks for movies, TVCs, animated films, and other media products, and effectively use AI tools such as text-to-speech engines and Adobe Audition’s AI-powered features.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of total class hours to be eligible for the final examination. - Actively participate in all class activities. - Complete all tasks assigned by the instructor after class. - Use personal laptops only for learning purposes during class time. - Read the textbook in advance before each session.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Explain the technical principles of audio production workflows and equipment, and relate these principles to the effective use of digital audio production tools.
Analyze sounds elements used in media products, such as cartoons, short films, TVC, and viral videos, to understand and evaluate the aesthetic and functions of sound.
Apply sound theories, methods, and technical equipment to perform audio correction, editing, and mixing tasks in Adobe Audition.
Use audio effects in Adobe Audition and apply AI tools to optimize efficiency in audio production across various media formats, including podcasts, cartoons, films, TVCs, and viral videos.
Design and produce audio for complete media products, and evaluate the quality, clarity, and effectiveness of the edited sound through appropriate effects and production techniques in Adobe Audition.
Demonstrate a professional working attitude, autonomy in task execution, and effective teamwork when performing sound design, editing, and production activities.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Lecturer assesses students’ TVC sound design developed in class. Students must complete a 1-minute TVC sound.
assessments.Grading Guide: - Record and process sound effects - Harmonize and mix audio elements for a TVC

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Lecturer assesses students’ animated film sound design developed in class. Students must complete a 10-second animated film sound.
assessments.Grading Guide: - Record and process sound effects - Harmonize and mix audio for an animated film

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Lecturer assesses students’ film sound design developed in class. Students must complete a 10-second film sound.
assessments.Grading Guide: - Record and process sound effects - Harmonize and mix audio for a film - Apply corrections, effects, and sound aesthetics

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Evaluation based on learners’ preparation, class interaction, and completion of practice tasks.
assessments.Grading Guide: Recording and processing sound effects in class activities.
